open_questions: Expensive and Ajala follow machine Songsterr tabs: tempo and form match the records, and a fold of each record agrees with the main groove, but the fills and the rarer bars are unchecked.
Ajala's intro: the tab writes only a hit on the 1 for 24 bars, but the record has percussion, and perhaps hat or rim, under it.

Quest for Coin (2019), Victory Dance, No Confusion and Life Goes On (2022), his best-known Afrobeat grooves, have no usable transcription (Victory Dance's two machine tabs are empty or garbled); not scored.
His handedness and which hand leads the hat: not stated in any source read; the footage looked at was too far off to say.
The Drum-Drops sample packs of his kit (recorded at Livingston Studios) are sold, not free, and their pages could not be read on 2026-10-26.

identity.name: Femi Koleoso
identity.summary: A Nigerian-British Londoner who started on the drums in church at four, came up through Tomorrow's Warriors and in 2012 founded Ezra Collective with his brother TJ, the band he leads from the kit. He took the overnight bus to Paris for lessons with Tony Allen, kit facing kit. Ezra Collective's Where I'm Meant to Be (2022) was the first jazz album to win the Mercury Prize; Dance, No One's Watching (2024) plays Fela's Expensive Shit and dance-floor grooves at 103 to 155. He also drums for Jorja Smith and in Gorillaz's live band.

traditions.impact: He started playing drums in church aged four (Jubilee Church, among the "building blocks of me").
Fela was his earliest influence, from his father's CDs; lessons with Tony Allen in Paris shaped "the foundation of the sound I was trying to create".
Tomorrow's Warriors; Ezra Collective began by imitating Blakey and Roach, then played standards "with a Fela Kuti Afrobeat way of playing the changes rather than swinging".
Making "a straight hip-hop beat swing, almost like a shuffle", after Karriem Riggins, Chris Dave and Clever Austin.

formative_events.event: Joined Tomorrow's Warriors, the youth jazz programme of Gary Crosby and Janine Irons, where he met the rest of Ezra Collective.
Lessons with Tony Allen in Paris, reached by overnight bus: kit opposite kit, copying his grooves for hours, then talking them through.
Founded Ezra Collective with his brother TJ on bass.
Where I'm Meant to Be won the Mercury Prize, the first jazz album to do so.

eras.label: Tomorrow's Warriors to You Can't Steal My Joy
eras.context: Ezra Collective's EPs, recorded at Abbey Road in an engineer's downtime (Chapter 7, 2016; Juan Pablo: The Philosopher, 2018), Quest for Coin and the debut album; drumming for Jorja Smith.

eras.label: Where I'm Meant to Be and Gorillaz
eras.context: Gorillaz's live band from 2020; Where I'm Meant to Be (2022), with No Confusion as a tribute to Tony Allen, and the Mercury Prize.

eras.label: Dance, No One's Watching
eras.context: Dance, No One's Watching (2024), the Brit Award for Group of the Year (2025) and arena concerts.
defining_traits: four on the floor under Afrobeat snare figures

genres.name: Afrobeat
genres.notes: Expensive (Fela), Ajala; No Confusion and his lessons with Tony Allen.

genres.name: R&B and soul
genres.notes: No One's Watching Me; Jorja Smith.

evidence.note: Locked in for a studio sound ("I don't want it to be loose ... I might even use a click"), a laid-back hip-hop shuffle on Footprints.

swing.notes: Straight sixteenths in all four songs scored here; swung hip-hop elsewhere (Footprints).

dynamics.balance: A big kick ("that beefy stadium sound" from double-ply heads), the snare and hat up front for dancing.

feel_profile.interaction: Leads the band from the kit; cues it back in from his solos with set fills ("certain drum fills let them know").

hand_techniques.name: The hat opened with the snare
hand_techniques.description: Ajala's hat opened on each stroke of the snare figure, over four on the floor at 155.

hand_techniques.name: Rim clicks off the beat
hand_techniques.description: No One's Watching Me's cross-stick on the "a"s of 1 and 2, on 4 and its "a", the hat on the "and"s.

foot_techniques.name: Four on the floor under Afrobeat
foot_techniques.description: The kick on every beat under snare figures in threes (Expensive, Ajala, God Gave Me Feet for Dancing).

coordination.notes: A kick ostinato (four on the floor, or the threes) under snare and cymbal figures that repeat in the bar.

searched: Songsterr 6427587 (Expensive), 3217003 (Ajala), 3080488 (God Gave Me Feet for Dancing), 3216852 and 2259170 (No One's Watching Me)
Reverb (2020), Hypebeast (2022), The Line of Best Fit (2022), 15 Questions (2022), his SABIAN profile
devices_search.note: No cross-rhythm, grouping, polymeter or metric modulation is named or written. The snare in threes (3+3+4+3+3 sixteenths) is a figure inside the bar that starts again on every 1, not a cycle across the bar line.

voice_language.hihat: Eighths in the Afrobeat heads, sixteenths in God Gave Me Feet for Dancing, opened with the snare in Ajala, on the "and"s in No One's Watching Me.
voice_language.snare: Figures in threes, not a backbeat: 1, the "a" of 1, the "and" of 2, the "and" of 3; rim clicks in the slow songs.
voice_language.kick: Four on the floor, or in threes (1, the "a" of 1, the "and" of 2, the "a" of 3, the "and" of 4) under a cowbell.
voice_language.cymbals: The ride's bell on the beat or in eighths over the kick in threes; crashes on the off-beats in God Gave Me Feet for Dancing.

aesthetic: A bebop-sized Ludwig with an 18" bass drum, the kick fattened with double-ply heads
Tuning changed mid-gig with Ezra Collective; held firm for Jorja Smith
For a J Dilla studio sound, the snare layered with claps or tambourine

sample_hints.afrobeat: A vintage Ludwig, warm and a little loose, the kick big.

signature_traits.label: The snare in threes over four on the floor
signature_traits.description: The snare on 1, the "a" of 1, the "and" of 2 and the "and" of 3 (3, 3, then 4 sixteenths) while the kick plays every beat: Fela's Expensive Shit and Ajala made for a dance floor.

signature_traits.label: A bell on the beat over the kick in threes
signature_traits.description: The cowbell, or the ride's bell, on every beat while the kick plays 1, the "a" of 1, the "and" of 2, the "a" of 3 and the "and" of 4: Expensive's bridge and its ride sections.

signature_traits.label: Tony Allen's student
signature_traits.description: Lessons with Allen in Paris, kit opposite kit; No Confusion (2022) is his tribute. Allen told him he barely had to move: "I can play the beats, but it's the sound and the groove that he could get, that's the life's work."

signature_traits.label: Leads the band from the drums
signature_traits.description: Bandleader and main voice of Ezra Collective on stage; his solos are improvised from whatever solo came before, and set fills cue the band back in.

patterns.name: Expensive, the head
patterns.function: Eighths on the hat, the snare on 1, the "a" of 1, the "and" of 2, the "and" of 3 and the "e" of 4, the kick on every beat: Fela's tune over four on the floor.

patterns.name: Expensive, the bridge
patterns.function: The cowbell on the beat, the kick in threes (1, the "a" of 1, the "and" of 2, the "a" of 3, the "and" of 4), the snare on the "and" of 1, the "e" and "a" of 2, the "and" of 3 and on 4.

patterns.name: Ajala, the groove
patterns.function: The hat opened with the snare on 1, the "a" of 1, the "and" of 2, the "and" of 3 and the "and" of 4, the snare on the "a" of 3 too, over four on the floor at 155.

patterns.name: God Gave Me Feet for Dancing, the verse
patterns.function: Sixteenths on the hat, the snare on the "a" of 1, the "and" of 2 and the "and" of 4, the kick on every beat.

patterns.name: God Gave Me Feet for Dancing, the snare figure
patterns.function: No hat: the snare on 1, the "and" and "a" of 1, the "and" of 2, 3, its "and" and "a", the "e" and "and" of 4, over four on the floor.

patterns.name: No One's Watching Me, the head
patterns.function: The hat on the "and"s and the "a" of 3, rim clicks on the "a" of 1, the "a" of 2, on 4 and its "a", the kick on 1, 3 and its "and".

equipment.label: Ludwig Classic Maple, the Ezra Collective kit (2020)
equipment.layout_notes: A kit "modelled on bebop drum kits", for solos that ring when quiet; thick double-ply heads on the bass drum. For Jorja Smith, a 20" Ludwig Keystone with an 18" and a 16" floor tom and a 12" rack tom, played to a click and backing track.

affiliations.name: Ezra Collective
affiliations.notes: Founded with his brother TJ out of Tomorrow's Warriors; You Can't Steal My Joy (2019), Where I'm Meant to Be (2022, Mercury Prize), Dance, No One's Watching (2024).

affiliations.name: Jorja Smith
affiliations.notes: Her band, including the 2018 Tiny Desk Concert.

affiliations.name: Gorillaz
affiliations.notes: The live band, through the 2022 world tour.

evidence.note: Lessons in Paris by overnight bus, kit facing kit; "Uncle Tony shaped the foundation of the sound I was trying to create" (Hypebeast, 2022).
"I was massively into Max Roach, Art Blakey" (Reverb, 2020).
"One of my biggest influences ... It's basically making a straight hip-hop beat swing."

philosophy.idea: A drummer should write the music: the drums are what everyone watches.
Learn a groove by sitting opposite it and copying, then talk it through, like a drum circle.
Never plan a solo's start: answer what was just played, or by the tenth night you are regurgitating.

contribution.description: Leads Ezra Collective from the drums, fusing Afrobeat, calypso, reggae and hip-hop with jazz; the band won the 2023 Mercury Prize, the first jazz act to do so, and was the first jazz band to win a Brit Award for Group of the Year. He carries Tony Allen's Afrobeat, learnt from Allen himself, to London dance floors.

innovations: Afrobeat snare figures over four on the floor, for jazz played to dancers

accolades.for: Where I'm Meant to Be, with Ezra Collective

accolades.award: Brit Award for Group of the Year

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A 1960s Ludwig, warm and a little loose, with a big kick
generation_rules: The snare in figures of threes, not on 2 and 4.
Four on the floor, or the kick in threes under a bell on the beat.
The hat in eighths, opened with the snare, or in sixteenths.
Straight, locked in, at dance tempos.

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Tony Allen's Afrobeat, learnt kit to kit in Paris, with Blakey's jazz and Dilla's hip-hop: London jazz for dancing.
